texts.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the colony's first winter while they worked, the version with the bear in it. {B_nameDef} has heard there was no bear. {B_nameDef} enjoyed it anyway.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} what the place looked like before the walls went up, and got the whole afternoon's answer, with names.
{A_nameDef} pointed out to {B_nameDef} where the first well was dug, where the first grave is and where somebody once fell in the river in front of everyone. It was {A_nameDef}.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: an old hand's correction

texts.li: {A_nameDef} watched {B_nameDef} work for a full minute without speaking, then took the tool out of {B_possessive} hands and showed {B_objective} the grip. It was a better grip. {B_nameDef} said thank you through {B_possessive} teeth.
"Not like that," {A_nameDef} said, and showed {B_nameDef} how {A_pronoun} was taught forty years ago. It worked. {B_nameDef} hates that it worked.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the trick of the job that nobody had thought to mention. {B_nameDef} will be doing it that way from now on, and pretending it was {B_possessive} own idea.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: shown the old way of it

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} sat on the bench by the wall and agreed that everything was better in their day, including the weather and the knees.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} compared aches over breakfast like traders comparing goods. {A_nameDef}'s back won. {B_nameDef}'s hip came a close second.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon remembering people nobody else here ever met, and laughing at things nobody else would understand.
{A_nameDef} fell asleep at the supper table halfway through a sentence. {B_nameDef} put a blanket round {A_possessive} shoulders and finished the sentence for {A_objective}, roughly.
{A_nameDef} dozed off in the sun with {A_possessive} work in {A_possessive} lap. {B_nameDef} quietly finished it and put it back. {A_nameDef} woke up and said it had gone faster than expected.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: an old game

texts.li: {A_nameDef} taught {B_nameDef} a game {A_pronoun} played as a child, with stones and lines scratched in the dirt. {B_nameDef} won the third game and has been unbearable since.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} how to make a whistle out of a blade of grass. {B_nameDef} has been whistling at everyone. {A_nameDef} pretends to regret it.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon at an old counting game with pebbles. {A_nameDef} let {B_nameDef} win, then stopped letting {B_objective}, and still lost.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: an old game in the dirt

texts.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef}, at length, everything wrong with young people today, using {B_nameDef} as the example throughout.
{A_nameDef} watched {B_nameDef} work and said "in my day we did it properly", and then didn't explain what properly was.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} a simple question and got a lecture about patience, respect and the state of the colony's boots.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: a saying that helped

texts.li: {B_nameDef} was fretting over a job gone wrong, and {A_nameDef} said "the best ploughman still turns a crooked furrow". {B_nameDef} laughed, and went back to it.
{A_nameDef} answered {B_nameDef}'s long complaint with one old saying. {B_nameDef} thought about it all afternoon, and admitted at supper it was right.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: a saying at the right moment

texts.li: {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} a straight question and got "every cloud has a silver lining" in reply. {B_nameDef} asked again. {A_nameDef} said "patience is a virtue". {B_nameDef} walked off.
{A_nameDef} said "many hands make light work" while watching {B_nameDef} do all of it. {B_nameDef} has had enough of the sayings.
{B_nameDef} sat at {A_nameDef}'s feet for an hour while {A_nameDef} told the one about the clever fox and the farmer's daughter. {B_nameDef} wants it again tomorrow, with the fox winning.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} a bedtime story with three dragons in it and no ending yet. {B_nameDef} has been following {A_nameDef} round all day asking for the ending.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: a laugh at the wrong moment

texts.li: {B_nameDef} was talking about the one {B_pronoun} lost, and {A_nameDef} laughed. Not at it. {A_nameDef} just laughed, the way {A_pronoun} does when things are hard. {B_nameDef} got up and left.
{A_nameDef} laughed at the graveside, quietly, into {A_possessive} sleeve. {B_nameDef} heard it, and hasn't spoken to {A_objective} since.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: a laugh at a sad time

texts.li: {B_nameDef} said {B_pronoun} had never promised to fix the fence. {A_nameDef} took out the notebook and read {B_objective} the date, the hour and the exact words. {B_nameDef} is fixing the fence.
{A_nameDef} corrected {B_nameDef}'s story at supper from the notebook, page and line. Everyone laughed except {B_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} was certain the roof would come down in the next storm. {B_nameDef} climbed up and checked every beam with {A_objective} watching from below. It won't. {A_nameDef} slept that night.
{B_nameDef} sat with {A_nameDef} and counted the stores out loud, sack by sack, until {A_nameDef} believed there was enough to last the winter.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: volunteered in their place

texts.li: {B_nameDef} was dreading the cesspit duty. {A_nameDef} took it before {B_nameDef} could finish complaining, and whistled the whole time.
{A_nameDef} volunteered for {B_nameDef}'s night watch when {B_nameDef} was tired. {B_nameDef} slept like a stone and woke up owing a favour.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: took a turn at the worst job

texts.li: {A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the half-wild cat {A_pronoun} has been feeding behind the storehouse. {B_nameDef} brought it a scrap too. The cat now has two people.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent an hour coaxing a frightened stray out from under the wagon. It bit them both. They were delighted.
{B_nameDef} blew out {A_nameDef}'s candle to save it, and {A_nameDef} lit it again, and {B_nameDef} blew it out, and so on until someone shouted at both of them.
{B_nameDef} complained that {A_nameDef}'s light keeps half the colony awake. {A_nameDef} said the dark keeps {A_objective} awake, and which was worse?
